name: Characterised Vietnamese food-strain set
what: Characterise 20 to 50 moulds and yeasts already used in Vietnamese ferments and held in public collections (Aspergillus oryzae from tuong; Rhizopus and Amylomyces from banh men; protein-rich yeasts such as Pichia kudriavzevii isolates): whole-genome sequence, toxin-gene and antibiotic-resistance screens, growth on cassava glucose and okara, protein content; publish the data and supply the strains on one standard licence with pre-agreed benefit-sharing terms under the Decree 43/2026 route
why_vietnam: VTCC holds over 15,000 strains, 3,869 documented and available to domestic users (SLF-01); 41 works on microbes of Vietnamese ferments but none on food-strain safety characterisation (SLF-03); a Vietnamese screen found a yeast with 62 to 67% protein and no safety data (SLF-04); Decree 43/2026 cut the access licence to about 19 working days at provincial level, but benefit sharing of at least 1% of product revenue still applies (SLF-02; REG-60); T9's first kill test is strain safety data; strains with a history of use in Vietnamese food fit P1's traditional-food lane
must_be_true: A host collection (VTCC or FIRI) agrees to standard licence and benefit-sharing terms; whole-genome sequencing and toxin screening can be bought at research-grant cost; at least three firms want characterised strains; MAE and provincial authorities accept a standard licence for strains supplied by public collections
kill_tests: Fewer than three firms request strains within a year of release; screened food strains carry toxin-gene clusters (cyclopiazonic acid, 3-nitropropionic acid) or acquired resistance with no clean alternatives; standard benefit-sharing terms for collection strains cannot be agreed
first_customers: T9 koji and fungal-food startups; YERA (yeast protein, Nghe An); Emmay (mushroom and mycelium foods); chay makers testing fermented ingredients; university groups such as Phenikaa University
partners: VTCC (VNU Hanoi Institute of Microbiology and Biotechnology); FIRI Industrial Microbiology Center; Institute of Biotechnology (VAST); MAE Department of Nature Conservation and Biodiversity; a provincial Department of Agriculture and Environment; NIFC for safety testing
capital_note: Not estimated; sequencing and screening tens of strains is a research-grant-scale project (our judgement, no quote retrieved)
